newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil panel delays telecom bill vote to next week.
newsitem.headline: Brazil panel delays telecom bill vote to next week.

text.p: A committee of the Brazilian Congress' lower house will only vote next week on a bill regulating and opening up the country's telecommunications sector, a panel member said.
"There have been last minute changes and the government, just like the opposition, needs to study them," said Deputy Benito Gama, the government's chief whip in the Chamber of Deputies.

The government had hoped the General Telecommunications Law would be approved Wednesday by the special lower house committee mulling the legislation. But opposition members argued they needed more time to study last minute changes in the bill.

One change would allow foreign investors to own a minimum 49 percent and maximum 100 percent of a Brazilian telecoms firm, with precise limits set on a case-by-case basis by the president, said Deputy Jose Aleluia of the government-allied Liberal Front party.
Gama said the special telecoms panel would probably meet again Tuesday for more discussion and a possible vote on the bill and its amendment.
If approved by the committee, the bill would go to the full Chamber of Deputies and then to the Senate for final approval.
